title: Posture Assessment Failure Trends
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Posture Assessment Failure Trends' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.

Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row.

description: Surfaces risk tied to Posture, Assessment, Failure, Trends through UC-17.1.11 on `index=nac` sourcetype `cisco:ise:posture`. Summarises `count` grouped by `failure_reason` across `1d` before applying -30d. Operators tune 'Posture Assessment Failure Trends' using UC-17.1.11 runbook steps.
value: Tracking `activity` via UC-17.1.11 on `cisco:ise:posture` feeds improves response to 'Posture Assessment Failure Trends' and reduces unauthorized access, segmentation drift, and NAC policy failures.
implementation: Normalize `failure_reason` from ISE. Alert when daily failures exceed 7-day baseline by >50%. Segment by AD group or location if extracted.
visualization: Line chart (failures over time by reason), Stacked area (failures by policy), Single value (failures vs prior week).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Certificate or EAP profile rollout** — Clients fail EAP-TLS during staged cert deployment for 'Posture Assessment Failure Trends'. Cross-check `FailureReason` and CMDB cert expiry.

2. **RADIUS/PSN maintenance restart** — Short auth failure burst while ISE node restarts. Match change window on `index=changes`.

3. **Guest or IoT onboarding surge** — Legitimate MAC registration spike skews `index=nac` `cisco:ise:posture` baselines.

4. **Approved pen-test or scanner traffic** — Red-team exercises from netblock in `approved_scanners.csv` mimic auth failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `CallingStationID`, `NAS-IP-Address`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco ISE Posture Module with AnyConnect ISE Posture Agent or Temporal Agent. Data in `index=nac` with `sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog`. Key fields: `PostureStatus`, `PostureAssessmentFailure` (specific check that failed), `PostureRemediation` (action taken), `OperatingSystem`, `UserName`, `CallingStationID`.
• ISE Posture checks include: antivirus (installed, running, definitions updated), anti-malware, Windows patches, disk encryption (BitLocker/FileVault), firewall status, registry keys, application presence.
• Each posture requirement has a remediation action (install update, enable feature) and a grace period.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Verify posture failure data:
```spl
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" PostureStatus=NonCompliant earliest=-7d
| stats count by PostureAssessmentFailure, OperatingSystem
| sort - count
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Primary search — Failure trend by check type:
```spl
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" PostureStatus=NonCompliant earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count by PostureAssessmentFailure limit=10
```

Understanding this SPL: Trends posture failures over 30 days. Spikes correlate with external events: AV definition updates that fail to deploy, Windows Patch Tuesday (second Tuesday of the month), or ISE posture policy changes that introduce new requirements. A sustained increase in a specific failure type means the remediation is not working — the posture agent cannot fix the issue automatically.

Remediation effectiveness:
```spl
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" earliest=-7d
| where PostureStatus="NonCompliant" OR PostureStatus="Compliant"
| sort CallingStationID _time
| streamstats current=f last(PostureStatus) as prev_status by CallingStationID
| where prev_status="NonCompliant" AND PostureStatus="Compliant"
| eval remediation_time_sec=_time - relative_time(_time, "-1h")
| stats avg(remediation_time_sec) as avg_remediation_sec dc(CallingStationID) as devices_remediated
```

Step 3 — Validate
(a) In ISE: Context Visibility > Endpoints > Compliance tab.
(b) Disable AV on a test device, reconnect, verify NonCompliant status appears.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard: Row 1 — Compliance rate trend. Row 2 — Failure types over time. Row 3 — Remediation effectiveness.
Alert: When any single posture check failure exceeds 50 affected devices in 24h.

Runbook:
1. **AV definition spike** — AV update server issue. Check WSUS/SCCM distribution point.
2. **Post-Patch-Tuesday spike** — Expected. Should resolve within 48h. If not, SCCM deployment stalled.
3. **New check introduced** — ISE posture policy change. Monitor the first 72h for impact.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **PostureAssessmentFailure field empty** — ISE may not log specific check names. Enable detailed posture reporting in ISE.
• **NonCompliant count always high** — Posture policy may be too strict. Audit each posture requirement for necessity.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk_TA_cisco-ise — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:posture into nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`failure_reason`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We track which security checks devices fail when they connect — like having antivirus out of date or missing patches — and watch for patterns. If many devices suddenly fail the same check, it usually means an update did not deploy correctly, and we can fix it before it becomes a bigger problem.
